transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it’s really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um, I guess I’m here because... well, I've just been having a little bit of trouble keeping things straight lately. It's probably nothing major, and I feel a little silly even bringing it up, but I just feel like I can't quite get my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. 

Like, my supplies, my due dates, receipts, and all my assignment notes... they kind of just always end up in these messy piles. And then I just look at them and I don't really know what to do first, so I get a bit stuck. I try really hard to keep on top of it all, I promise, but it just gets a bit overwhelming. Is that... is that an okay reason to come in? Does that make sense?
Did you have this same kind of trouble staying organized when you were a child?

Um... well, honestly, I don't remember the messy piles as much back then, but my teachers definitely noticed... other things. It wasn't because I was trying to be difficult or anything! I was just really eager, I think. 

My mom actually still has some of my old elementary school notes, and, um, they usually said I was always out of my seat, or that I'd start talking before the teacher even called on me. And I guess I tended to rush through group activities a lot, even when I completely understood the work. I just... I liked to move fast, you know? I was just a really enthusiastic kid. 

Does... does that answer your question? I'm sorry if that's not exactly about being organized, I just hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.
When you’re working on something important, do you often find your mind drifting and have trouble staying focused on it?

Um, a little bit, maybe? I mean, I think everyone’s mind wanders sometimes, right? 

But, um... like, if I'm in class, or if I have to watch a lecture video for my business assignments, I really do start out listening. I try my best to be a good student! But then, after just a few minutes, my brain kind of... well, it just gets really excited about my shop. I'll start thinking about new charm designs, or fun ideas for packing my orders. And before I know it, I realize I kind of missed half of what was just said in the video. 

I always try to go back and figure out what I missed, I promise! It's not that I don't care about the work, I just have a really active imagination, I think. Is that... is that the kind of drifting you mean?
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking things, even when you already know they’re fine?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I definitely try to make sure I pack all my orders correctly, because I really want my customers to be happy! But once I check something and know it's right, I'm usually good to go. 

I don't think I get stuck checking the same thing over and over again, if that makes sense? Like, I might be a little messy sometimes, but I don't really have that kind of... repetitive checking thing going on. I hope that's a good thing?
When you put off starting a task, is it usually because you get distracted by other thoughts or activities?

Um... well, I don't really put things off very often! I try really hard to stay on top of my assignments and my shop orders, I promise. 

If I do ever delay starting something, it's usually just because I'm... well, maybe I'm just being really thorough and thinking about the best way to do it? Or sometimes I just have so much creative energy that I want to finish a quick sketch for a new charm before I sit down to do my homework. It's not that I'm trying to avoid the work, I just get really inspired sometimes! 

Does that make sense? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses or being lazy. I really do try my best to get everything done!
Do these organization and focus problems also cause trouble in other parts of your life, like at home or in relationships?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try not to let it affect anyone else, I promise! I hate letting people down. 

But, um... well, recently, I guess I kind of missed a few required steps for my school program. It was just an honest mistake, I just lost track of the dates! But now they're saying my financial aid might be at risk, which is really scary. I'm trying to fix it, I really am! 

And, um, with my shop... I sometimes collaborate with other creators, which is so much fun! But lately, I think they've started depending on me a little less for the shared projects. I think maybe I was just a little too scattered for them, or maybe I missed a few too many messages while I was brainstorming. I don't want them to think I'm unreliable, because I really do care! 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds really bad, doesn't it? I really am trying to be better about all of it, I promise. I just... I get so caught up in things sometimes. Is that... is that really terrible?
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different parts of your life, even when there isn’t a clear reason to worry?

Um, oh, no, I don't think so! I mean, I definitely get a little stressed when there's an actual problem—like the financial aid thing I just mentioned—because I really, really want to fix it and make things right. 

But I don't just sit and worry for no reason, I promise! I try to be a really positive person. Usually, I'm just too busy doing things or, um, bouncing around with new ideas for my shop to get stuck worrying about stuff that isn't even happening. I really try to look on the bright side of things and just keep moving forward. 

Is that... I mean, I hope that's a good answer? I'm definitely not a worrier!
Did these problems get noticeably worse after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

Um, well... I guess I wouldn't say there was one huge, terrible event or anything! I mean, I've always been a little energetic and scattered, but I always tried my best to keep it together. 

But I guess... maybe it started getting a little harder to manage about, um, two years and two months ago? That's when I changed schools. And, well, I started this new business program, and I was also trying to run my accessories shop at the same time. The new school just didn't have as much structure as I was used to, and I had to figure out a lot of things on my own. 

I really tried to handle it all, I promise! I didn't want anyone to think I couldn't do it. But it was just... a lot of balls to keep in the air without someone kind of pointing me in the right direction. Does that make sense? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm blaming the school, because I know I should be able to manage my own time. I just... I guess that's when things started slipping a little bit. Is that the kind of change you meant?
Before you changed schools, were these focus and organization problems already causing you trouble?

Um, well... yeah, I guess they kind of were? But I really wasn't trying to be difficult or anything, I promise! I just... well, my mom actually still has some of my old notes from my elementary school teachers. 

And, um, they used to write that I was always getting out of my seat, or, you know, talking before I was called on. And I guess I would kind of rush through group activities a lot, even when I totally understood the work! I didn't mean to mess up the groups, I just got so excited to participate or to see what the next fun thing was going to be, you know? 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid, because I always wanted to do a good job and make my teachers happy! I just had so much energy back then... and I guess I still do! Is... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
